task.question: In which Japanese city was the 2025–26 Grand Prix of Figure Skating Final held, where Alysa Liu won the women's singles title?
task.evidence: held from December 4 to 7 at the Aichi International Arena in Nagoya, Japan.
task.page: 2025–26 Grand Prix of Figure Skating Final

answer:
The **2025–26 Grand Prix of Figure Skating Final** was held in **Nagoya, Japan**, specifically at the Aichi International Arena, from December 4 to 7. It was there that **Alysa Liu** of the United States won the women's singles title.

FINAL: Nagoya

messages.content: [2025–26 Grand Prix of Figure Skating Final] The 2025–26 Grand Prix of Figure Skating Final and the 2025–26 Junior Grand Prix of Figure Skating Final were figure skating competitions, sanctioned by the International Skating Union (ISU), and organized and hosted by the Japan Skating Federation (Japanese: 日本スケート連盟). The Grand Prix Final was the culminating event of the 2025–26 Grand Prix of Figure Skating series, as was the Junior Grand Prix Final the culmination of the 2025–26 Junior Grand Prix series. Both events were held concurrently from December 4 to 7 at the Aichi International Arena in Nagoya, Japan. Medals were awarded in men's singles, women's singles, pair skating, and ice dance at the junior and senior levels. Ilia Malinin and Alysa Liu of the United States won the senior men's and women's events, respectively. Riku Miura and Ryuichi Kihara of Japan won the senior pairs event, and Madison Chock and Evan Bates of the United States won the senior ice dance event. Seo Min-kyu of South Korea won the junior men's event, Mao Shimada of Japan won the junior women's event, Guo Rui and Zhang Yiwen of China won the junior pairs event, and Hana Maria Aboian and Daniil Veselukhin of the United States won the junior ice dance event.

messages.content: [Alysa Liu] Alysa Liu ( ə-LISS-ə LEE-oo; born August 8, 2005) is an American figure skater. She is the 2026 Olympic champion in both the women's singles and team events, the 2025 World champion, the 2022 World bronze medalist, the 2025–26 Grand Prix Final champion, a two-time Grand Prix medalist, a four-time Challenger Series champion, and a two-time U.S. national champion. At the junior level, Liu was the 2020 World Junior bronze medalist, the 2019–20 Junior Grand Prix Final silver medalist, a two-time Junior Grand Prix champion, and the 2018 U.S. junior national champion. In 2019, Liu, then 13, became the youngest-ever U.S. women's national champion. The following year, she became the youngest skater to win two senior national titles, the first woman to win consecutive U.S. titles since Ashley Wagner in 2012 and 2013, and the first girl to win the junior and senior titles back-to-back since Mirai Nagasu in 2008. Following a period of retirement, she won a world title at the 2025 World Championships, becoming the first U.S. woman to do so since Kimmie Meissner in 2006. At the 2026 Winter Olympics, she became the first American woman to win an individual medal since Sasha Cohen in 2006, as well as the first American gold medalist since Sarah Hughes in 2002. An accomplished jumper, Liu was the first woman to complete a quadruple jump and a triple Axel in the same program, and the first to land a triple Axel-triple toe loop combination in the short program. She was the first American woman to land a quadruple jump and the first American junior woman to complete a triple Axel in international competition.
